summary: PARTIAL holds. PR #710 (60633eff3) fixed persistence. The 40 ms full rewrite is now a 1 s trailing window per session, with write-through on clear, restart, close and exit, a flush on shutdown, and readHistory doing a single read with no rewrite. It also added an I/O-gated back-off to the subprocess poll: 1 s for 5 ticks after any I/O, then 5 s. No spawn-free detection exists, and no implementation was found elsewhere: PtyAdapter has no foreground API and no other module replaces the snapshot. Every server with a live shell still spawns `/bin/ps -eo pid=,ppid=` (powershell Get-CimInstance on Windows) every 5 s when idle and every 1 s while any terminal has output. A live shell can exist even if the drawer was never opened, because ProjectSetupScriptRunner opens one for worktree setup scripts. The auditor's subscriber-gating option is weaker than it implies. Every connected client subscribes to all terminal events at connect time (connection.ts:320, wsRpcClient.ts:577), and worktreeSetupProgress subscribes on the server, so gating would only save spawns on headless nodes with no attached client.

evidence.note: DEFAULT_PERSIST_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1_000. In f1be4abc7 it was 40 (per the git show 60633eff3 diff).

queuePersist keeps one pending window per session and reads the latest historyState.history when the window ends. Superseded windows are dropped at 1292. The output path calls it at 1704 only for visible text.
A finalizer flushes and drains pending windows on shutdown, with a 5 s cap. Tests at Manager.test.ts:1355-1429 cover window coalescing, exit write-through and shutdown flush.
readHistory does a single readFileString (NotFound maps to none) and caps in memory only. The old exists check and rewrite-on-cap are gone.
appendTerminalHistoryChunk appends incrementally (string concat at historyBuffer.ts:183). Only the 1 s window does the full-file writeFileString (1264).
DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000, the back-off the proposal suggested.

subprocessPollTick skips a spawn only when there was no I/O for 5 ticks. I/O is bumped by output (1651), PTY start (1915), input (2353) and activity change (2117). Continuous output (dev server log, top, a TUI) still means 1 spawn/s, the same as before. Tested by Manager.test.ts:1431.
Effect.forever(waitForRunningSession -> tick -> sleep 1 s) runs for as long as any session is 'running'. The loop is not gated on subscribers.

snapshotPosixProcessTable is still a ps -eo pid=,ppid= spawn. snapshotWindowsProcessTable (668) spawns powershell.exe Get-CimInstance Win32_Process at the same cadence, which costs far more per spawn. Windows (nsis) is a desktop build target.
PtyProcess exposes only pid, write, resize, kill, onData and onExit. It has no foreground-process or tcgetpgrp API, so spawn-free detection was not implemented anywhere.
The server opens a shell terminal for worktree setup scripts and the shell stays alive afterwards. The poll can therefore run for the server's lifetime even if the user never opened the drawer.
Every connection subscribes to all terminal events (subscribeTerminalEvents replay 'metadata', wsRpcClient.ts:577). Subscriber-count gating would only help when no client is attached.

A server-side consumer of 'activity' events (added in #728) that relies on the poll to settle the setup-script stage. Any gating or cadence change must keep it working. Its comment at :37 still says '~1s poll'.
processTableSnapshotFailing logs once per failure streak. This fixes the side issue of a warning every second on truncated ps output.

An existing long-lived native sidecar already samples pid and ppid without fork/exec (sample(), cached for 1 s). It is a possible spawn-free snapshot source where it is bundled. Unused by the terminal manager.

remaining: Polling still spawns a process. Every server with at least one running shell runs subprocessPollTick (Manager.ts:2105-2125), which spawns `/bin/ps -eo pid=,ppid=` (Manager.ts:637-666), or powershell Get-CimInstance on Windows (Manager.ts:668-700). The rate is about 0.2/s when idle and 1/s for as long as any terminal produces output, plus 5 s after that. Long-running noisy processes (dev servers, watchers, top, TUIs) keep the 1/s rate indefinitely, so the proposal's '-1 spawn/s' is only reached when terminals are idle (-0.8/s). Persistence still rewrites the full file (up to 2 MiB) at most once per second per terminal under sustained output, not O(chunk). That matches the proposal's explicitly offered alternative and is acceptable.
fixDefects: No defects found in the implemented fixes. The shutdown finalizer ordering is correct: the session-kill finalizer runs first, then the persist flush, before workerScope and the persist worker are torn down, and this is covered by a test. Back-off interaction checked: a foreground command ending prints a prompt, which bumps I/O, so the next 1 s tick polls. Foreground end detection, including the worktree setup-script watcher, stays at about 1 s. Only silent background-job exits are delayed by up to 5 s, which is a documented trade-off (Manager.ts:92-97). One nit: worktreeSetupProgress.ts:37 says '~1s process-table poll'. That is accurate for the cases it handles but does not mention the idle cadence.
implementationSketch: Preferred, with no semantic change: make the poll edge-triggered instead of periodic during output. In Manager.ts, replace the ticksSinceIo scheme in subprocessPollTick (2099-2125) with explicit triggers: (1) on input or PTY start (noteTerminalIo at 1915 and 2353), poll on the next tick plus one or two follow-ups (catches false->true when a command starts); (2) on output, do not poll every tick but arm a trailing quiet timer of about 300-500 ms per manager, and poll once when output goes quiet (catches true->false because the shell prints a prompt and then goes quiet); (3) keep a slow sweep (raise DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS to 10-15 s) only for silent background-job changes. Optionally skip the sweep when terminalEventListeners.size === 0, and run a fresh pollSubprocessActivity when a subscription starts or listDiagnostics is called, so headless nodes with no attached client stop spawning entirely and reattaching clients still get fresh hasRunningSubprocess. Optional spawn-free source: add an optional `snapshotFromNativeMonitor` processTableSnapshotter that maps nativeResourceMonitor.sample() (NativeResourceMonitor.ts:406) to childrenByParent when health is 'healthy' and the shell pids are in the retained set, falling back to ps or powershell. This matters most on Windows. A foreground-only variant (Linux: read /proc/<shellPid>/stat tpgid; macOS: sysctl KERN_PROC_PID e_tpgid or node-pty IPty.process behind a new optional PtyProcess.foregroundProcessGroup()) removes spawns entirely but stops detecting background jobs. Tests: extend Manager.test.ts:1431 (TestClock plus a counting processTableSnapshotter) with (a) continuous emitData for 10 ticks, asserting at most 1-2 snapshots, then quiet, asserting exactly one trailing snapshot; (b) write() followed by an activity event within 1 tick; (c) the idle sweep count at the new interval; (d) no listeners means no sweep snapshots, and subscribing triggers one. Keep watchSetupScriptTerminal behaviour covered: script starts, then ends with a prompt, and the stage settles within about 1 s. Update the comment at worktreeSetupProgress.ts:37.
decisionReason: The recommended edge-triggered poll keeps today's semantics: foreground start and end are still detected within about 1 s. A longer idle sweep only delays silent background-job exits, which is already an accepted trade-off. Only the foreground-only spawn-free variant (tcgetpgrp or node-pty process) changes semantics, because background jobs go undetected, and that would need explicit product sign-off.
correction: Auditor's classification and evidence are accurate. Additions: (1) subscriber gating is less effective than implied, because every connected client subscribes globally (connection.ts:320) and worktreeSetupProgress subscribes on the server, so it only helps headless nodes; (2) a live shell can exist without the drawer ever opening, through ProjectSetupScriptRunner.ts:53; (3) the same loop spawns powershell Get-CimInstance on Windows, which is much more expensive per tick; (4) an existing NativeResourceMonitor sidecar is an unused, already-shipped option for a source that needs no ps/powershell spawn per poll.
